root_cause.text: ext4_mb_release() incorrectly tied discard-work draining to the current EXT4_MOUNT_DISCARD mount flag, so after a remount to nodiscard it could skip flushing previously queued s_discard_work and leave s_discard_list work pending during teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` guard and makes `flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work);` and `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&sbi->s_discard_list));` unconditional, while the CVE/commit explicitly states that after mounting with discard, queuing `s_discard_work`, then remounting with nodiscard, “the pending s_discard_work is neither cancelled nor flushed.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Always flush discard work and verify the discard list is empty during ext4_mb_release() so all ext4_free_data is drained regardless of the DISCARD option.
intent_record.what: The conditional block `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD)) { ... }` around `flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work);` and `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&sbi->s_discard_list));` was removed, making the comment and both calls unconditional in `ext4_mb_release()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `ext4_mb_release()` now always waits for `s_discard_work` to finish and always checks that `s_discard_list` is empty before proceeding, regardless of whether the DISCARD mount option is enabled. This ensures queued `ext4_free_data` associated with discard work is drained during release and avoids leaving pending discard-related state behind when DISCARD is disabled.

grouping_result.intent: Always flush discard work and verify the discard list is empty during ext4_mb_release() so all ext4_free_data is drained regardless of the DISCARD option.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by making ext4_mb_release() always flush pending discard work and check that the discard list is empty, instead of depending on the current DISCARD mount flag after remount.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the root cause: it gates discard-work draining on the current mount DISCARD option, so after remounting with nodiscard, previously queued discard work is not flushed during ext4_mb_release().

This is the required draining operation, but in the vulnerable code it executes only under the DISCARD mount-flag check, allowing pending s_discard_work to be skipped when the filesystem was remounted nodiscard.

This verification of pending discard items is also incorrectly made conditional on the current DISCARD option, so teardown can miss and fail to detect leftover s_discard_list entries after remount to nodiscard.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the root cause because it makes teardown draining of previously queued discard work depend on the current DISCARD mount option. After remounting with nodiscard, ext4_mb_release() skips flushing s_discard_work and checking s_discard_list, leaving pending ext4_free_data work during teardown.

    ext4: get discard out of jbd2 commit kthread contex
    
    Right now, discard is issued and waited to be completed in jbd2

    amount of files are deleted and discard is flooding, jbd2 commit
    kthread can be blocked for long time. Then all of the metadata

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant teardown logic is shown directly in ext4_mb_release(), so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present in the conditional drain of discard work: `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD)) { flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work); WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&sbi->s_discard_list)); }`. This ties flushing of `s_discard_work` and checking `s_discard_list` to the current mount option `DISCARD`. From the same diff, discard work can be queued earlier in `ext4_process_freed_data()` via `list_splice_tail(&freed_data_list, &sbi->s_discard_list);` and `queue_work(system_unbound_wq, &sbi->s_discard_work);` when discard was enabled at that time. If the filesystem is later remounted with `nodiscard`, then `test_opt(sb, DISCARD)` becomes false during `ext4_mb_release()`, causing teardown to skip `flush_work()` even though previously queued discard work and list entries may still exist. That matches the stated root cause. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not yet present because release does not unconditionally drain discard work/list independent of the current mount flag.

In this commit's `ext4_mb_release(struct super_block *sb)` body, there is no discard-work logic at all: no check of a discard mount flag, no `EXT4_MOUNT_DISCARD`, no `s_discard_work`, no `s_discard_list`, and no workqueue draining or cancel/flush operation. The function only releases committed blocks and allocator metadata, e.g. `list_splice_init(&sbi->s_closed_transaction, &sbi->s_committed_transaction);`, `ext4_mb_free_committed_blocks(sb);`, cleanup of group info, buddy cache, proc entries, and locality groups. Because the vulnerable construct is completely absent in this version, this function does not contain the bug. Likewise, the later fix is also not present here, since there is no unconditional flushing/draining of discard work during teardown.
